title: Surge in desperate Aussies tapping super
full_text:
The amount of superannuation released on compassionate grounds has nearly tripled, climbing from $472.4m to more than $1.4bn in the five years to July 2025, as One Nation calls for more flexibility to allow struggling Aussies access to their retirement savings.
Data on the early compassionate release of super from the Australian Taxation Office also reveals that applications have more than doubled between 2020-21 to 2024-25, rising from 45,300 to 112,400 – an increase of 148 per cent.
Australians are allowed to apply on compassionate grounds for the early release of their super in five situations – for medical treatment and medical transport; to prevent the forced sale of a home; for palliative care; for funeral expenses, and for reasons related to severe disability.
Super released to prevent the foreclosure or forced sale of a home nearly tripled from $7.2m in 2020-21 to $20.9m in 2024-25, while amounts related to funeral costs and palliative care remained steady.
Money released for medical treatment also more than tripled from $447.4m in 2020-21 to $1.369bn in 2024-25.
One Nation’s treasury spokesman Barnaby Joyce said the party would release a superannuation policy ahead of the next election – due by 2028 – however said he did not want to lower the current 12 per cent superannuation guarantee for employers. Shadow Treasurer Tim Wilson said the increase in early withdrawals showed more Australians were “tapping their super to keep their head above water”.
